title: What makes a receipt the IRS will accept
label: 1-minute bookkeeping fix

items.s: Card or bank statement, canceled check.

items.t: Photo it the day you buy

cta.sub: We'll DM you the expense tracker.

captions.instagram:
Not every scrap of paper proves a business expense. The IRS lists what a good record shows.

✔️ Who you paid, how much, and the date.
✔️ Proof you paid: a card or bank statement, a canceled check or a receipt.
✔️ What it was for, so it's clearly a business expense.
✔️ Electronic records follow the same rules as paper ones.

The habit: take a photo the day you buy, and add the business reason.

Our Business Expense Tracker sorts each one into its Schedule C category.
captions.youtube_title: Will the IRS Accept This Receipt? What a Good Record Shows
captions.youtube_description: IRS: supporting documents for business expenses should show who you paid, the amount, the date, proof of payment (card or bank statement, canceled check, receipt) and a description that shows the business purpose. Electronic records follow the same rules as paper. Photograph receipts the same day and note the business reason.
captions.pinterest_title: What Receipts Does the IRS Accept? Small Business Receipt Rules Explained
captions.pinterest_description: Receipt organization for small business taxes: the IRS says supporting documents should show who you paid, the amount, the date, proof of payment and the business purpose. Card statements, canceled checks, invoices and register receipts all count, and electronic records follow the same rules. Photo every receipt the day you buy.
captions.pinterest_alt: Short video listing what an IRS-ready receipt or record shows, with a myth vs fact on digital copies.

ads_keywords: what receipts does the irs accept

sources.fact: Supporting documents for expenses: canceled checks/proof of payment, cash register receipts, account statements, credit card receipts and statements, invoices; they should show payee, amount, proof of payment, date and a description showing business purpose; requirements for paper records also apply to electronic records (page updated 03-Aug-2026); read 2026-10-30
